comparison: Both evaluate in vivo CF suppression (C23-C26, C62-C65, C91-C95). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to regional mismatch (lobule IV/V vs flocculus), incomplete penetrance (75%), and limited duration validation (40 min vs hours-long experiments). Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging new in vivo data but noting it 'fails to address overall concerns' about functional effects and long-duration efficacy.

Both evaluate CF role in memory retrieval (C37, C71, C101-C102). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on within-subject design and consistent null results, noting only that brief testing may miss some aspects. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns about CF suppression efficacy and selectivity that apply across all behavioral phases.

Both evaluate CF necessity for acquisition (C3, C28-C32, C66-C69, C96-C98). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with strong statistical evidence (p=0.0007) and clear behavioral phenotype, noting limitation to gain-increase learning. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with editor stating 'there is evidence to support' this claim and reviewers acknowledging 'impacts on behavior are interesting,' though requesting clearer demonstration of manipulation penetrance and selectivity.

Both address in vitro optogenetic validation (C17-C22, C103-C104). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on 100% success rate, appropriate controls, and strong statistics. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'climbing fiber activity was altered due to the optogenetic perturbation,' though the in vitro data itself was not directly challenged.

Both evaluate CF role in consolidation (C4, C33-C36, C70, C99-C100). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on lack of group differences across two consolidation durations, noting limitation to early windows (up to 6 hr). Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with editor stating 'support for the latter part of the claim is incomplete' due to methodological concerns about CF suppression efficacy, tissue damage, and the unanswered question of what signal instructs consolidation if not CFs.

Both evaluate the overall phase-specific model (C5, C39-C40, C43-C44). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on convergent evidence across acquisition, consolidation, and retrieval phases. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with editor stating 'there is evidence to support the first part [acquisition] but support for the latter part [consolidation] is incomplete' due to methodological concerns, and one reviewer noting 'substantial new experiments and tighter logic are required.'

Both evaluate claims about downstream circuit independence (C38, C72). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the conclusion is 'largely inferential' without direct MVN measurements or manipulation. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, with one reviewer criticizing the 'narrow CF-or-nothing framing that leaves unanswered the central question of which signal instructs consolidation if CFs do not.'

Both address viral targeting specificity (C15-C16). OpenEval includes these claims in a SUPPORTED evaluation of in vitro optogenetic effects. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with significant concerns about selectivity: 'viruses chosen are non-specific to the cell targets,' 'unclear if AAVs labeled only the pathway of interest,' and requests for 'high-resolution images demonstrating selectivity and expression.'

OpenEval evaluates context-dependent CF function model (C45, C73-C74, C80-C81) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is 'largely interpretive' without systematic variation of error magnitude. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation linking optogenetic suppression to CF-LTD and plasticity (C54-C57) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is 'speculative' without direct measurements of calcium transients or LTD. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates alternative mechanisms from literature (C51-C53, C79) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are not tested in current study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based alternative mechanisms.

OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for claims accurately describing scope and limitations of consolidation experiments (C58-C60, C82-C83), noting 'honest assessment' of temporal window. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these limitation acknowledgments.

OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for background/context claims (C1-C2, C6-C14, C27, C42, C46-C50) as 'well-established knowledge' appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational context claims.

OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for methodological details (C84-C90) as 'technically sound' and consistent with prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically for these surgical/methodological claims, though peer reviewers raised broader concerns about viral targeting.

OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN for broader mechanistic models (C75-C77) as 'largely speculative' without direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these broader theoretical claims.
